title: Board-pattern readiness test — most-repeated question types
chapter: CBSE Class 10 Social Science (087) · History: India and the Contemporary World II · Crash revision (2026-27)
tagline: Practice questions modelled on past CBSE papers; not predictions of this year's paper.
disclaimer: Original questions written from this video's script, its worksheet and the NCERT/CBSE material it cites, modelled on most-repeated / high-weightage question types in CBSE Sample Question Papers and past board papers. Practice for readiness only: not predictions of any exam and no promise of marks.
instructions: 39 questions. MCQ and assertion-reason: choose one option. Numeric: type a whole number.

patterns.T7: Civil Disobedience: who joined and why

S1.name: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
S1.tip: Make a dated chain: 1789 → 1804 Civil Code → 1815 Vienna → 1821/1832 Greece → 1834 Zollverein → 1848 Frankfurt → Italy 1859–70 → Germany 1866–71. For 5-markers, one date and one leader per point.
S1.ncert: NCERT India and the Contemporary World II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 1 The Rise of Nationalism in Europe

S2.name: Nationalism in India
S2.tip: Learn the sequence 1917 Champaran → 1919 Rowlatt/Jallianwala → 1920 Calcutta/Nagpur → Jan 1921 NCM → Feb 1922 withdrawal → 1928 Simon → 1929 Lahore → 6 Apr 1930 Dandi → 1931 Gandhi-Irwin → 1932 Poona Pact. Know who joined CDM and why.
S2.ncert: NCERT India and the Contemporary World II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 2 Nationalism in India

S3.name: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3)
S3.tip: Only the pre-modern world is in the board paper. Two examples per 2-marker: silk routes (goods, Buddhism), food (potato, maize, chilli), smallpox, silver from Peru and Mexico.
S3.ncert: NCERT India and the Contemporary World II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 3 The Making of a Global World, sections 1 to 1.3 only

S4.name: Print Culture and the Modern World
S4.tip: Dates: 1430s Gutenberg, 1517 Luther, 1558 Index, 1780 Hickey, 1878 Vernacular Press Act. Link print to the Reformation and the French Revolution; match writers to works.
S4.ncert: NCERT India and the Contemporary World II (Reprint 2026-27), Ch 5 Print Culture and the Modern World

S5.name: History Map Work
S5.tip: Learn each map place with its year and reason: Calcutta & Nagpur 1920, Madras 1927, Champaran, Kheda, Ahmedabad, Jallianwala Bagh (Amritsar), Dandi (Gujarat coast).
S5.ncert: CBSE Social Science Curriculum 2026-27 map list (History: Nationalism in India); SQP 2026-27 Q9

questions.question: Which of these was a provision of Napoleon's Civil Code of 1804?
questions.explanation: The 1804 Code abolished privileges by birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It gave all women the right to vote
It did away with privileges based on birth and established equality before the law

questions.question: The Treaty of Vienna of 1815, hosted by Metternich, aimed mainly to:
questions.explanation: The Bourbons were restored and conservative regimes imposed censorship: the aim was to undo Napoleon's changes.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Spread the ideas of the French Revolution
Undo most of the changes made during the Napoleonic wars

questions.question: The Zollverein, formed in 1834 at the initiative of Prussia, was:
questions.explanation: The customs union removed tariff barriers and cut the number of currencies from over thirty to two, helping economic unity.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: A customs union that abolished tariff barriers and reduced over thirty currencies to two
A parliament elected by all adult men
A secret society to unify Italy
A treaty that ended the Greek war of independence

questions.question: In the unification of Italy, who led the Red Shirts?
questions.explanation: Mazzini founded Young Italy; Cavour used diplomacy; Garibaldi led the Red Shirts; Bismarck led German unification.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: In the allegory of Germania, the crown of oak leaves stands for:
questions.explanation: Germania = Germany; her crown of oak leaves symbolises heroism (Marianne stands for France).
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Arrange in the correct order: (i) Frankfurt Parliament meets (ii) Greek war of independence begins (iii) William I proclaimed German Emperor (iv) Zollverein formed
questions.explanation: 1821 Greek war → 1834 Zollverein → 1848 Frankfurt Parliament → January 1871 William I at Versailles.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and R is the example that explains A; the Napoleonic Code also reduced women to the status of minors.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: In nineteenth-century Europe, equality before the law did not mean universal suffrage.
questions.reason: In revolutionary France, the right to vote and to get elected was given only to property-owning men.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Why did the Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 fail to unite Germany?
questions.explanation: The king's rejection left the middle-class parliament without power; it was also narrow (women only as observers).
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The Prussian king Friedrich Wilhelm IV rejected the crown it offered, and the parliament lost the support of the powerful

questions.question: How was nation-building in Britain different from that in Italy and Germany?
questions.explanation: Britain's nation-state grew gradually (for example, the Act of Union of 1707) rather than by sudden upheaval.
questions.remediation: Video part 1: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It was achieved by Garibaldi's army
It happened in one war in 1871
It was imposed by the Treaty of Vienna
It was a long-drawn-out process, not the result of a sudden revolution

questions.question: Gandhiji's Champaran satyagraha of 1917 was organised for:
questions.explanation: Champaran (Bihar), 1917: peasants against the plantation system. Ahmedabad mill workers and Kheda peasants followed in 1918.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Peasants struggling against the oppressive plantation system

questions.question: Why was the Rowlatt Act of 1919 opposed?
questions.explanation: Detention without trial for two years: Gandhiji called a hartal on 6 April 1919.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It gave Indians more seats in councils
It allowed the detention of political prisoners without trial for two years

questions.question: Arrange in order: (i) Nagpur session adopts non-cooperation (ii) Champaran satyagraha (iii) Jallianwala Bagh massacre (iv) Movement withdrawn after Chauri Chaura
questions.explanation: 1917 Champaran → 13 April 1919 Jallianwala → December 1920 Nagpur → February 1922 withdrawal.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, the import of foreign cloth fell from ₹102 crore to ₹57 crore between 1921 and 1922. By how many crore rupees did it fall?
questions.explanation: 102 − 57 = 45 crore rupees: the value of imports nearly halved.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; the violence (R) is why Gandhiji called off the movement (A).
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Gandhiji withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement in February 1922.
questions.reason: The movement was turning violent in many places, as at Chauri Chaura.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Who formed the Swaraj Party after the Non-Cooperation Movement ended?
questions.explanation: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru wanted to return to council politics; Nehru and Bose wanted more radical mass agitation.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Chandra Bose
C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru

questions.question: What did Gandhiji's march to Dandi, which reached there on 6 April 1930, begin?
questions.explanation: 78 volunteers walked about 240 miles; breaking the salt law at Dandi began Civil Disobedience.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The Civil Disobedience Movement, by breaking the salt law

questions.question: Which groups stayed lukewarm towards the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Rich peasants, business classes and women joined; dalits and many Muslims stayed lukewarm.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which statement best describes the role of Indian business classes in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
questions.explanation: Business groups (FICCI, formed in 1927) wanted protection from imports and supported the movement financially.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: They formed the Swaraj Party in 1930
Industrialists like Purshottamdas Thakurdas and G. D. Birla gave financial help and refused to buy or sell imported goods
They opposed it from the start and supported British imports
They led the salt march to Dandi

questions.question: What did the Poona Pact of September 1932 provide?
questions.explanation: Ambedkar's demand for separate electorates ended in the Poona Pact: reserved seats, general electorate.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Reserved seats for the depressed classes, to be voted in by the general electorate
Separate electorates for the depressed classes
An end to the salt tax

questions.question: For plantation workers in Assam, what did 'swaraj' mean?
questions.explanation: Swaraj meant different things to different groups; for Assam plantation workers, it meant freedom to move.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: The right to move freely in and out of the plantations and keep in touch with their villages
Getting seats in the legislative council

questions.question: Why was the Simon Commission met with the slogan 'Go back Simon' in 1928?
questions.explanation: The all-British commission was boycotted with 'Go back Simon'.
questions.remediation: Video part 2: Nationalism in India; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It did not have a single Indian member
It wanted to give India Purna Swaraj

questions.question: The name 'silk routes' points to:
questions.explanation: The routes linked Asia with Europe and northern Africa; Chinese silk going west gave them the name.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Routes used only by silk farmers
The west-bound Chinese silk carried along them

questions.question: Which of these foods came to Europe and Asia from the Americas?
questions.explanation: Potatoes, maize, tomatoes and chillies came from the Americas; noodles may have travelled west from China.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which religion spread from eastern India along the silk routes?
questions.explanation: Trade and culture went together: Buddhism spread along the silk routes.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true, and the lack of immunity explains why germs did more damage than guns.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Smallpox was the Spanish conquerors' most powerful weapon in America.
questions.reason: America's long isolation meant its people had no immunity against diseases from Europe.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: What was the role of silver from mines in present-day Peru and Mexico?
questions.explanation: American silver made Europe richer and paid for Asian goods.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It ended trade on the silk routes
It was used only to make coins in China
It enhanced Europe's wealth and financed its trade with Asia
It caused the Irish potato famine

questions.question: Why did the centre of world trade shift westwards towards Europe after the fifteenth century?
questions.explanation: China's withdrawal from overseas contact, plus Europe's sea routes and silver, moved the centre of trade west.
questions.remediation: Video part 3: The Making of a Global World (1 to 1.3); then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Europe closed its ports to Asia
The silk routes were paved with gold
China restricted its overseas contacts, while Europe gained new sea routes and American wealth

questions.question: What was the first book printed by Johann Gutenberg?
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's first book was the Bible, about 180 copies; his system was perfected by 1448.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Martin Luther's Ninety Five Theses of 1517 led to:
questions.explanation: Luther's criticism of Church practices, spread by print, began the Reformation; the Church responded with the Index of Prohibited Books (1558).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Which writer and work are correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Phule wrote Gulamgiri (1871); Rashsundari Debi wrote Amar Jiban (1876); Rammohun Roy published Sambad Kaumudi; Tilak wrote in Kesari.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: What did the Vernacular Press Act of 1878 do?
questions.explanation: Modelled on Irish press laws, it allowed censorship of the vernacular press; nationalist papers still grew.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: It gave the government extensive powers to censor reports and editorials in the vernacular press
It started English printing in India
It made printing free for all newspapers

questions.question: Arrange in order: (i) Hickey's Bengal Gazette (ii) Index of Prohibited Books (iii) Gutenberg's press perfected (iv) Luther's Ninety Five Theses
questions.explanation: By 1448 Gutenberg → 1517 Luther → 1558 Index → 1780 Hickey.
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Many historians argue that print helped create the conditions for the French Revolution. Which reason supports this?
questions.explanation: Enlightenment ideas, debate and satire of royalty undermined the monarchy (Mercier: 'tremble, therefore, tyrants of the world').
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.
options: Print spread the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers, a culture of debate, and literature that mocked royalty
Print made all French people literate overnight
The king owned all printing presses

questions.question: Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Both true; his fear of a flood of worthless and harmful books (R) explains his unease (A).
questions.remediation: Video part 4: Print Culture and the Modern World; then the worksheet practice for this part.
questions.assertion: Erasmus was not happy about the spread of printed books.
questions.reason: He feared that print would flood the world with worthless books.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

questions.question: Jallianwala Bagh, a place on the CBSE History map list, is in:
questions.explanation: 13 April 1919: General Dyer fired on a crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: History Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: At which Congress session, in September 1920, was the decision to start non-cooperation taken?
questions.explanation: Calcutta, September 1920: decided; Nagpur, December 1920: adopted.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: History Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: Champaran, marked on the map list for Gandhiji's 1917 satyagraha, is in present-day:
questions.explanation: Champaran is in Bihar (indigo plantation peasants); Kheda and Ahmedabad are in Gujarat.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: History Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: A place on the Gujarat coast where Gandhiji broke the salt law on 6 April 1930 is:
questions.explanation: Dandi: end of the salt march; Civil Disobedience began there.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: History Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.

questions.question: On a map, place A is clued 'satyagraha of 1918 for cotton mill workers' and place B 'Congress session of 1927'. Identify A and B.
questions.explanation: Ahmedabad (mill workers, 1918) and Madras (Congress session, 1927) are both on the CBSE map list.
questions.remediation: Video part 5: History Map Work; then the worksheet practice for this part.
